understand.title: Todo App with Filters
what: A todo list where you can add, tick, delete and edit todos, and filter them: All / Active / Completed.
It shows how many todos are left and keeps them in localStorage, so a refresh does not lose them.
where: The most common first React round (30–45 min). They watch how you shape state.
Task lists, cart lines, inbox filters: the same add / toggle / filter shape.
contract: text input labelled New todo and a button Add (Enter also adds)
each todo has a checkbox whose label is the todo text, and a button labelled Delete <text>
buttons All, Active, Completed
text N items left (1 item left for one)
double-click the text → input labelled Edit <text>, Enter saves
save to localStorage under the key todos
rules: Blank text is not added
The visible list is computed from todos + filter, not stored in state
Use a stable id as key, never the index

☐ Buy milk        ✕
☑ R̶e̶a̶d̶ ̶d̶o̶c̶s̶       ✕
[All] [Active] [Completed]   1 item left

quiz.q: Where should the list of visible todos (after the filter) live?
opts: In its own useState, updated on every filter click
why: It can be calculated from state you already have. A second copy goes out of sync the moment you add or delete a todo.

quiz.q: You use the array index as key. You tick todo #2, then delete todo #1. What goes wrong?
opts: Nothing, index keys are fine for lists
React throws a key warning and stops rendering
React reuses DOM by position, so local DOM state (like an open edit input) can jump to the wrong todo
The deleted todo stays on screen
why: After a delete every index shifts by one. React matches old and new items by key, so it thinks item 1 changed instead of item 0 being removed. Anything kept in the DOM or in child state follows the position, not the todo.

understand.title: Accordion
what: A list of sections. Each section has a header button and a panel. Clicking the header opens or closes its panel.
Two modes: single (opening one closes the others) and multiple (each opens on its own).
where: FAQ pages, settings groups, filters in a sidebar.
Tests props design, state shape (one id vs a list of ids) and ARIA.
contract: props: items = [{ id, title, content }], multiple (default false), defaultOpen (array of ids)
each header is a <button> with the title as its text and aria-expanded
each panel has role="region", is labelled by its header, and the header's aria-controls is the panel id
a closed panel is hidden (hidden attribute or not rendered)
rules: Keep one piece of state: the list of open ids
Use a real <button>: Enter and Space then work for free

quiz.q: Which state shape supports both single and multiple mode with the least code?
opts: A boolean isOpen inside each item object in props
why: An array of ids works for both. Single mode just replaces it with [id]; multiple mode adds or removes. A single number can only hold one open panel.

quiz.q: Why use a <button> for the header instead of a <div onClick>?
opts: A button is focusable and fires click on Enter and Space, and screen readers announce it
Only buttons can have aria attributes
why: A div needs tabIndex, a key handler and a role to match what a button gives for free.

understand.title: Modal / Dialog
what: A dialog that sits on top of the page. It renders into document.body with a portal, so parent overflow or z-index cannot clip it.
It closes on Escape and on a backdrop click, locks page scroll, keeps focus inside while open, and gives focus back to the button that opened it.
where: Confirm delete, login popups, image preview.
Checks portals, effects with cleanup, refs and keyboard/focus handling.
contract: props: open, onClose, title, children
when open is false, render nothing
the dialog has role="dialog" and aria-modal="true", labelled by the title
the backdrop has data-testid="backdrop"; a close button labelled Close
while open: document.body.style.overflow = "hidden", restored on close
rules: Clicks inside the dialog must not close it
Tab and Shift+Tab cycle only inside the dialog
First focusable element gets focus on open

quiz.q: The modal is rendered with createPortal(…, document.body). A click inside it bubbles to…
opts: Only document.body, because that is its DOM parent
Its React parents too, because React events follow the component tree
why: React events bubble through the React tree, not the DOM tree. An onClick on a parent component still sees clicks from inside the portal.

quiz.q: You lock scroll in a useEffect. What must the cleanup do?
opts: Restore the old body.style.overflow and remove the keydown listener
why: Everything the effect changes outside React must be undone in cleanup, or the page stays unscrollable and the listener leaks.

what: A row of stars. Click a star to set the rating. Hovering previews a rating; moving the mouse away shows the real value again.
It is controlled: the parent owns value and gets changes through onChange. A readOnly mode shows stars without any interaction.
where: Product reviews, feedback forms, course ratings.

container: role="radiogroup"
each star: role="radio", name 1 star, 2 stars…, aria-checked true on the star equal to value
a filled star shows ★, an empty star shows ☆

readOnly: no hover preview, clicks do nothing

quiz.q: Which value decides how many stars look filled?
why: While hovering, show the preview; when hover is cleared (null), fall back to the real value. Math.max would make it impossible to preview a lower rating.

understand.title: Tabs
what: A row of tabs; one panel shows at a time. Arrow keys move between tabs, Home/End jump to the first/last.
Panels are lazy: a panel is rendered only after its tab was opened once, then it stays mounted (hidden), so its state is kept.
where: Settings pages, product details (Description / Reviews / Specs), dashboards.
Keyboard handling, roving tabindex, ARIA roles and lazy mounting.
contract: props: tabs = [{ id, label, content }], defaultTab (id, default first), orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical")
role="tablist" with aria-orientation; each tab role="tab" with aria-selected; panels role="tabpanel"
only the selected tab has tabIndex=0, others -1
horizontal: ArrowRight/ArrowLeft (wrap around); vertical: ArrowDown/ArrowUp; Home/End. Moving also selects and focuses the tab
inactive visited panels stay in the DOM with the hidden attribute; never-visited panels are not rendered
rules: State: the active id + the set of visited ids

quiz.q: What does "roving tabindex" mean in a tab list?
opts: Only the selected tab is in the Tab order (0); arrows move between tabs
The tablist itself is focusable, tabs are not
why: One Tab press enters the widget, the next leaves it. Inside, arrow keys move. That is the pattern screen-reader users expect for tabs, menus and radio groups.

quiz.q: Why keep a visited panel mounted with hidden instead of unmounting it?
opts: It renders faster the first time
Its state (typed input, scroll, fetched data) survives switching tabs
Hidden elements are not in the DOM
why: Unmounting throws away component state. Mounting lazily and then hiding gives both: no work for unseen tabs, no lost state for seen ones.

understand.title: Countdown Timer
what: A timer that counts down from a number of seconds and shows MM:SS. Buttons: Start, Pause, Reset.
At zero it stops and calls onComplete once. Pause and resume must not drift: compute time from a fixed end time, not by counting ticks.
where: OTP resend timers, quiz timers, sale countdowns, Pomodoro apps.
The classic "setInterval in React" question: cleanup, stale closures, drift.
contract: props: seconds, onComplete
the time text MM:SS is in an element with role="timer"
buttons Start, Pause, Reset
no interval is left running after unmount
rules: Reset stops the timer and shows the full time
onComplete fires exactly once

quiz.q: You write setInterval(() => setLeft(left - 1), 1000) in an effect with [] deps. What happens?
opts: It goes from 60 to 59 and stays there
It counts down twice as fast
why: The callback closed over left from the first render (60). Every tick sets 59. Fix with setLeft(l => l - 1) or by computing from an end time.

quiz.q: Why compute the remaining time from endTime - Date.now() instead of subtracting 1 every tick?
opts: Intervals are not exact (background tabs, busy main thread), so counting ticks drifts
why: Browsers delay timers, especially in background tabs. A fixed end time keeps the display right no matter how late a tick arrives.

import { act, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'
import TrafficLight from './TrafficLight'

beforeEach(() => vi.useFakeTimers())
afterEach(() => vi.useRealTimers())

const wait = (ms) => act(() => vi.advanceTimersByTime(ms))
const now = () => screen.getByRole('status').textContent
const lit = () => [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-on="true"]')].map((b) => b.dataset.color)
const press = (name) => fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name }))

test('starts on red with one bulb lit', () => {
  render(<TrafficLight />)
  expect(now()).toBe('Red')
  expect(lit()).toEqual(['red'])
  expect(document.querySelectorAll('[data-on="false"]')).toHaveLength(2)
})

test('cycles red 3s → green 3s → yellow 1s → red', () => {
  render(<TrafficLight />)
  wait(2999)
  expect(now()).toBe('Red')
  wait(1)
  expect(now()).toBe('Green')
  wait(3000)
  expect(now()).toBe('Yellow')
  expect(lit()).toEqual(['yellow'])
  wait(1000)
  expect(now()).toBe('Red')
})

test('Pause freezes, Resume restarts the current colour', () => {
  render(<TrafficLight />)
  wait(2000)
  press('Pause')

what: A hook that runs commands. Each command knows how to execute and how to undo itself. The hook keeps a past stack and a future stack.

understand.title: Error Boundary
what: A class component that catches errors thrown while rendering its children and shows a fallback instead of a blank page. It reports the error and has a Try again button.
A useErrorHandler hook sends async errors (from effects, promises, event handlers) to the nearest boundary, because boundaries cannot catch those by themselves.
where: Around widgets, routes and the whole app so one bug does not white-screen everything.
Why it must be a class, what boundaries cannot catch, and resetting.
contract: default export class ErrorBoundary with props fallback (a node, or a function ({ error, reset }) => node), onError(error, info), resetKeys (array)
without fallback: a role="alert" with Something went wrong and a button Try again
onError gets the error and info.componentStack
reset (button or reset()) clears the error and renders the children again; a change in any of resetKeys also resets
named export useErrorHandler() → a function (error) => void that makes the error reach the boundary
rules: Use getDerivedStateFromError for the fallback and componentDidCatch for reporting
understand.result:
┌ Something went wrong ─────────┐
│ Cannot read 'name' of null     │
│ [Try again]                    │
└────────────────────────────────┘   (rest of the page still works)

quiz.q: Which error does an error boundary NOT catch by itself?
opts: An error thrown while rendering a child
An error in a child's constructor
An error inside a setTimeout or a promise .then
An error in a child's render 3 levels down
why: Boundaries only see errors during React's render and commit. Async code runs later, outside that. Re-throw it during render with a setState trick: that is what useErrorHandler does.

understand.title: Custom Hooks Library
what: Six small reusable hooks: useDebouncedValue, useLocalStorage, useClickOutside, useWindowSize, usePrevious and useIntersection.
Each one cleans up its timers and listeners, and returns stable functions.
where: Every codebase has a hooks folder like this. Libraries: usehooks-ts, react-use.
"Write a custom hook for X" is a very common question.
contract: one file hooks.js with named exports
useDebouncedValue(value, delay): returns value once it stopped changing for delay ms
useLocalStorage(key, initial) → [value, setValue]: reads JSON on mount, writes on change, supports setValue(prev => …), the setter is stable, and a storage event for the key (another tab) updates it
useClickOutside(ref, handler): mousedown outside ref.current calls handler; listener removed on unmount
useWindowSize() → { width, height }, updates on resize
usePrevious(value): the value from the previous render (undefined at first)
useIntersection(ref, options) → true / false from an IntersectionObserver; disconnects on unmount
rules: Every effect that adds something returns a cleanup that removes it

quiz.q: In usePrevious, why update the ref inside useEffect and not during render?
opts: Refs cannot be written during render
The effect runs after the render, so during the render the ref still holds the old value
why: Render reads ref.current (old value) and returns it; after commit the effect stores the new value for next time.

quiz.q: Why should setValue from useLocalStorage keep the same identity across renders?
opts: Callers put it in effect deps or pass it to memoised children; a new function every render would re-run them
why: Wrap it in useCallback with stable deps (or use the functional state update), like React's own setState.
